name: Voice coach / speech therapy
lead: Voice coaching and speech therapy are professional services used to change how a voice sounds or functions, and they are the route people take to a deeper, clearer, more resonant or more authoritative voice. Voice therapy is provided mainly by speech-language pathologists, who target vocal parameters such as vocal fold closure, pitch, volume and quality, chiefly to manage voice disorders but also to change overall voice quality, as in transgender voice therapy.[1][3] Vocal pedagogy, taught by voice teachers, is the related field focused on singing.[1][2]

The looks chain is about presentation: a voice with lower pitch, chest resonance and steady breath support is read by listeners as more masculine and confident, and it can match or strengthen the impression a face and physique give. In transgender voice therapy, masculinization work centres on chest resonance, larynx height and breath support, while lowering pitch emphasises a comfortable range rather than strain.[3]

On T Nation, a 2006 thread asking how to lower the voice drew the reply to see a voice coach or speech therapist.[4] Published evidence on voice therapy is described as limited and varies by method; no studies were found testing coaching for appearance goals in people without voice disorders.[1][3]
infobox: Resonant voice therapy, Accent Method, vocal hygiene

paras: Voice therapy orientations include symptomatic, physiologic, hygienic, psychogenic and eclectic approaches, and treatment is individualised to the disorder and the person.[1] Techniques include the Accent Method (diaphragmatic breathing with rhythmic vowel play), chant-talk, resonant voice therapy, REST exercises and vocal hygiene advice.[1]
Voice teachers build technique across breath, phonation, resonance, articulation and range, and may also teach microphone use and performance skills.[2]

Transgender voice therapy is the best-documented use of therapy to shift voice character. Voice acts as a social cue to sex and gender: formant frequencies, which relate to resonance, matter alongside pitch in how listeners perceive a voice, and nonverbal communication such as posture and gesture may matter even more.[3]

For pitch lowering, therapy emphasises a comfortable range rather than strain, along with breathing, warm-ups, relaxation and chest resonance. Practice moves from sustained sounds to conversation, with clinicians and clients setting goals together.[3] Surgical options such as cricothyroid approximation and laryngoplasty also exist.[1]

No studies found on coaching for appearance in healthy people. Within speech pathology, systematic reviews of resonant voice therapy (Yiu and colleagues, 2016) and of voice therapy for dysphonia (Drake and colleagues, 2016) exist, and one 2013 paper questioned its effectiveness for children's vocal fold nodules.[1] For transgender voice therapy, a 2012 review found that most studies were at the lowest level of the evidence hierarchy, though people who undergo therapy report high satisfaction.[3]

claims.claim: A voice coach or speech therapist can help lower or change a man's voice
claims.believers: A T Nation reply to a question on lowering the voice recommends seeing a voice coach or speech therapist.[4]
claims.experts: Voice therapy targets pitch, resonance and breath support, with evidence described as limited and mostly from voice-disorder and transgender-care settings.[1][3]

card.summary: Professional voice therapy or coaching to change how a voice sounds; real clinical field, but no appearance trials.
card.note: Evidence for voice therapy is mainly in voice disorders, not appearance.

quick.overview:
Voice coaching and speech therapy are professional services, from speech-language pathologists or voice teachers, for changing voice quality or function.

Evidence is mainly in voice disorders and is described as limited; none tests appearance goals in healthy people.
quick.mechanism: Therapists and teachers work on breath, pitch, resonance and vocal fold closure through guided exercises.
quick.risks: No notable harms are documented in the reviewed references.

chain: Work with a speech-language pathologist or voice teacher
Change pitch, resonance and breath support
angle.text: People use professional coaching to change the sound of their voice, working on pitch range, chest resonance and breath support so their voice matches the impression they want to give.
